name: Dynasort
summary: Shopify app that re-sorts collections, variant lists, search results and upsell blocks automatically, using recipes built from 60+ signals such as sales, margin, inventory and reviews.
best_for: Shopify stores with large or fast-changing catalogues where product order is a merchandising decision — seasonal ranges, frequent stock-outs, wide margin spreads — and nobody who wants to re-order collections by hand every week.
skip_if: your catalogue is small enough for one person to curate in an afternoon, the order barely changes, or you are not on Shopify — at $99 a month for the first paid tier, the sorting has to be earning its fee
honest_knock: Sorting driven by 60+ blended signals is powerful and opaque in the same breath: a recipe that ranks by margin, velocity and stock at once will sometimes bury a product you wanted seen, and there is real trial and error in getting the recipes to match how you actually merchandise. The jump from free to paid is steep at $99 a month, and it buys capacity rather than capability: search, recommendations and post-purchase are already in the free Demo, and Basic multiplies collections, recipes and serves (100,000 a month against 10,000). Above that the listing contradicts itself — the $249 card says 'Everything in Pro, plus' and the $499 card 'Everything in Basic, plus' — so which tier carries A/B testing and the connector API is not something the page settles. And the evidence base is thin: 4.6 from 15 reviews, with fourteen fives and a single one-star and nothing in between. It is Shopify-only, so it is not an option if any part of your catalogue lives elsewhere.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-read 3 October 2026 on apps.shopify.com/dynasort) Four tiers, all billed in USD and recurring every 30 days, and the cards have been rewritten since September. Demo is free for as long as you like: search, recommendations and post-purchase included, 2 collections sorted round the clock, 10 recipes drawn from 60+ signals, 2 managed collections, 10,000 serves a month, 7 days of serving analytics and a re-sort every 60 minutes. Basic is $99 a month for 25 sorted collections, 20 recipes, 10 managed collections, 100,000 serves a month, Customers Also Bought recipes, 7-day analytics and a 30-minute re-sort. The two upper cards are printed in a way that cannot be right as it stands: the card priced at $249 and named Pro opens with 'Everything in Pro, plus' and lists 1,000 collections, 250 recipes, 100 managed collections, unlimited serves, a 10-minute re-sort, 365-day analytics and priority onboarding, while the $499 Enterprise card opens with 'Everything in Basic, plus' and lists 100 collections, 50 recipes, 25 managed collections, 1 million serves a month, A/B testing with a one-click winner, a connector API, mobile-versus-desktop analytics, a 20-minute re-sort and 30-day analytics. Read by the headings, the 100-collection list belongs to Pro and the 1,000-collection list to Enterprise, the same swap we recorded on 14 September and saw corrected on 15 September; but the prices sit where they sit, so have the developer confirm which allowance comes with which price before you pay. Every paid tier carries a 30-day free trial. The September cards' yes/no lines for custom attributes, partner integration and product boost no longer appear.
